issues.body: parseShapeRows deduplicates solely by `(targetClass, path)` and keeps the first SPARQL result row. Multiple node/property shapes may legally constrain the same class/path with different `sh:minCount`, `sh:class`, `sh:datatype`, or `sh:name`, and shapesQuery has no ordering that makes the retained row deterministic. A later required constraint can therefore be discarded and shown as optional; class/datatype metadata can likewise vary by engine/result order. This silently makes the shape-aware picker inaccurate despite the PR's claim that suggestions reflect what shapes declare. The existing test only duplicates an identical required constraint, so it cannot detect the failure.
issues.fix_hint: Merge all rows for each `(targetClass, path)` deterministically instead of first-row-wins. At minimum OR `required`, preserve compatible class/datatype/name information with a documented deterministic conflict policy, and add a test where the first row is optional and a later duplicate has `minCount=1` (plus conflicting metadata if only one value can be represented). Alternatively retain separate constraints and merge them explicitly in mergeSuggestions.
issues.title: Duplicate SHACL constraints are discarded in arbitrary result order

verdict.summary: The query-builder lowering and handoff are broadly well tested, but SHACL suggestion parsing is nondeterministic and can silently misrepresent constraints when multiple shapes describe the same target-class/path pair. This conflicts with the feature's central shape-aware honesty claim and needs correction before approval.
